x: "Quack," or as his American friends call him, Max Quackenbos (Jnr.), sends an interesting letter giving news of the American Indoor Season. Dodds won five One Mile Races, slowest 4.10.6, fastest 4.08.3. The coloured boys almost monopolised the sprints.

This time was three seconds faster than Wooderson's schoolboy record, and compares favourably with the schoolboy times of American stars, such as Cunningham's 4m. 24.7s., MacMitchell's 4m. 21.1s., Dodds' 4m. 28.4s., Lash's 4m. 30.5s., and Zamperini's 4m. 21.2s.

Our successful members are to be congratulated on excellent performances and it is indeed a good sign to see one of our athletes putting in such good work in the Pole Vault which to Belgrave has been a Cinderella event since the pre-war days of Dodds.
